ig_carousel_topic.topic: CLV (closing line value) and why sharps obsess over it
ig_carousel_topic.slide1_text: Why do sharp bettors care more about the closing line than the result?
ig_carousel_topic.slide2_text:
Most bettors judge a bet by whether it won.
That's the wrong measure.
A bet can win and still be a bad bet. It can lose and still be a correct one.
ig_carousel_topic.slide3_text:
Closing line value is the real signal.
If you bet a team at +150 and the line closes at +120, you got the better number.
The market moved against your position. That means the crowd and sharp money agreed with you after the fact.
ig_carousel_topic.slide4_text:
Concrete example:
You bet Cleveland +162 on Monday morning.
By tip-off, the line has moved to +140.
You beat the close by 22 cents. That's positive CLV.
Over hundreds of bets, consistent positive CLV predicts long-term profit better than win rate alone.
ig_carousel_topic.slide5_text:
A 54% win rate with negative CLV is fragile. A 51% win rate with consistent positive CLV is sustainable.
The line is the market's best estimate. Beating it repeatedly is the actual edge.
ig_carousel_topic.caption: Win rate gets the attention. Closing line value tells the real story. If you're not tracking CLV, you're missing half the picture.
